q: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of generative tasks. What key challenge about them do the authors point to?
a: understanding the mechanisms that prevent their memorization of training data and allow generalization

q: Studying the role of the training dynamics, the authors identify two distinct timescales. What happens at the early one?
a: models begin to generate high-quality samples

q: Of the two training timescales the authors identify, what emerges beyond the later one?
How does the later of the two timescales change with the training set size n?
How does the early timescale change with the training set size n?
What does the dependence of the two timescales on the training set size n create?
a: a window of training times, growing with n, where models generalize effectively

q: When does overfitting disappear at infinite training times?
a: only when the training set size n becomes larger than a model-dependent threshold

q: These findings reveal a form of implicit dynamical regularization in the training dynamics. Even in what kind of settings does it allow models to avoid memorization?
The authors support their results with numerical experiments on realistic and synthetic datasets. Which architectures do these experiments use?
What model does the authors' theoretical analysis use?
a: a tractable random features model, studied in the high-dimensional limit
